mainTopic: Whether a מתעסק on שבת is פטור, the order of planned acts, and why stoking coals might bring one חטאת or two.
overview: רב אושעיא challenges שמואל's rule that everyone agrees a מתעסק on שבת is פטור. He argues that רבי יהודה's grapes-and-figs case seems to repeat the two Shimons' view, so maybe רבי יהודה holds a מתעסק is חייב. The גמרא answers that everyone agrees a מתעסק is פטור. Instead, the opinions differ about a picker who forgot his plan (שכח מלקט מלבו): the Shimons limit the argument to two categories, while רבי יהודה says it applies to one category too. רבא gives another answer: the difference is someone who did his planned acts in the reverse order, and a ברייתא about two candles supports the idea that order matters. Next comes a ברייתא about stoking coals on שבת: the תנא קמא says one חטאת, while רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק says two, for putting out the top coals and lighting the bottom ones. The גמרא asks what case fits both opinions. רבי אלעזר and רבי חנינא, backed by רבי יוחנן, explain it as a blacksmith (נפח), and say the argument is whether מקלקל בהבערה is חייב. A second explanation, from אמי בר אבין and רב חנניא בר אבין, begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב אושעיא quotes the view of the two Shimons
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא opens his objection by quoting רבי שמעון שזורי and רבי שמעון: the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע is only about a mistake between two categories.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא objects. רבי שמעון שזורי and רבי שמעון say: they did not argue about a mistake within one category, because there he is liable. They argued about a mistake between two categories, where רבי אליעזר obligates a חטאת and רבי יהושע exempts.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא is setting up a challenge to שמואל. First he quotes one opinion from the משנה so he can compare it to רבי יהודה's opinion in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the two Shimons, mixing up two items of the same category makes him חייב according to everyone. The only argument is when the two items belong to two different categories. This quote is the measuring stick for the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: one category or name (the two items count as the same kind)
two categories or names (the two items count as different kinds)
obligates him to bring a sin-offering

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya raised an objection:
phrases.notes: His objection is aimed at שמואל, who said earlier that everyone agrees a מתעסק on שבת is exempt.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמְרִים:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon Shezuri and Rabbi Shimon say:
They did not disagree about a matter
phrases.notes: 'They' means רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע in the משנה.

phrases.english: that is of one category, that he is liable;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא מִשּׁוּם שְׁנֵי שֵׁמוֹת,
phrases.english: rather, about a matter that is of two categories,
where Rabbi Eliezer obligates a sin-offering,
and Rabbi Yehoshua exempts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens an objection against שמואל's earlier ruling that a מתעסק on שבת is פטור according to everyone.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that everyone agrees a מתעסק on שבת is פטור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This step only sets up the source. The attack comes once רבי יהודה's view is compared to it.

steps.title: What does רבי יהודה add?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יהודה's case of grapes and figs is simply two categories, he is saying the same thing as the two Shimons. So what is he teaching?
steps.simpleTranslation: What does רבי יהודה say they argue about? About someone who meant to pick grapes and picked figs, or meant to pick black ones and picked white ones. But grapes and figs, black and white, are two categories! That is exactly the view of the two Shimons. What is רבי יהודה coming to teach us?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא points out that רבי יהודה's case looks identical to the two Shimons' case. That leaves no clear reason for רבי יהודה's opinion to exist.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grapes versus figs, and black versus white, are treated here as two categories. Then רבי יהודה and the two Shimons would be saying the same thing. Since a separate opinion in the משנה should teach something new, there must be a real difference between them.

keyTerms.meaning: to pick or harvest (a forbidden מלאכה on שבת)
what is he coming to teach us?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda, what is he saying that they disagree about?
About one who intended to pick grapes and picked figs,
or intended black ones and picked white ones.

phrases.aramaic: עֲנָבִים וּתְאֵנִים, שְׁחוֹרוֹת וּלְבָנוֹת, מַאי נִיהוּ?
phrases.english: Grapes and figs, black and white, what are they?
Two categories?

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי!
phrases.english: Then that is the same as Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Shimon Shezuri!
What is Rabbi Yehuda coming to teach us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares רבי יהודה's view to the two Shimons' view quoted in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רבי יהודה's case is simply a two-category mistake
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On that reading, רבי יהודה's view is identical to the two Shimons' view, so his statement would add nothing.

steps.title: Suggestion: רבי יהודה holds a מתעסק is liable
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא concludes that the difference must be about a מתעסק: רבי יהודה says חייב, and the Shimons say פטור. This contradicts שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't the difference between them about a מתעסק? רבי יהודה holds a מתעסק is liable, and רבי שמעון שזורי and רבי שמעון hold a מתעסק is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא proposes what the real argument must be. If he is right, שמואל's claim that 'everyone agrees' falls apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יהודה must be adding something, רב אושעיא suggests he holds that acting without awareness still makes one חייב. That makes the מתעסק question a real argument among the תנאים. It directly contradicts שמואל, who said everyone exempts a מתעסק on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: someone who does an action without intending that act (unaware)

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it that the difference between them is about one acting unawares?
That Rabbi Yehuda holds one acting unawares is liable,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי סָבְרִי: מִתְעַסֵּק פָּטוּר?
phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon Shezuri hold that one acting unawares is exempt?
phrases.notes: 'Hold' is plural here: it means רבי שמעון שזורי together with רבי שמעון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 in a way that turns into a challenge against שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל: everyone agrees a מתעסק on שבת is פטור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יהודה holds a מתעסק is חייב, then not everyone agrees, and שמואל is contradicted.

steps.title: No: everyone agrees a מתעסק is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב אושעיא's suggestion. All agree a מתעסק is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that one acting unawares is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by denying that רבי יהודה holds a מתעסק is חייב. It still has to explain what the argument is actually about, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof against שמואל only worked if the מתעסק question was the only possible difference between the opinions. By rejecting that, the גמרא takes on the job of finding a different difference. Step 5 supplies it.

phrases.english: No. One acting unawares: everyone agrees he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion of step 3 that רבי יהודה holds a מתעסק is חייב.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the תנאים argue about whether a מתעסק is liable
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes the מתעסק question is the only possible difference between רבי יהודה and the Shimons, but another difference exists.

steps.title: The real argument: a picker who forgot his intention
steps.stepSummary: The argument is about a picker who forgot his original plan (שכח מלקט מלבו). רבי שמעון שזורי holds that within one category, everyone says he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, this is what they argue about. רבי שמעון שזורי holds: if the picker forgot his intention, and the items are of one category, everyone agrees he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation of the argument that has nothing to do with מתעסק. It begins laying out רבי שמעון שזורי's view, and the explanation continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a picker whose mind shifted: he first wanted one fruit, then forgot and thought he wanted another, and then picked the first one. This is not a מתעסק, because he did intend to pick. So the question of a מתעסק's liability is no longer the argument, and שמואל is safe.

keyTerms.meaning: the picker forgot his original intention
and here, it is about this

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse 'שכח מלקט מלבו' with מתעסק. The forgetful picker still meant to pick fruit; he only lost track of which fruit he wanted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps שמואל's rule intact: on שבת, a מתעסק is פטור according to everyone.

phrases.english: And here, it is about this that they disagree:
Rabbi Shimon Shezuri holds:
If the picker forgot his intention,
phrases.notes: Literally 'forgot from his heart.' He first wanted one fruit, then thought he wanted another, and ended up picking the first.

phrases.english: with one category, everyone agrees he is liable,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the alternative difference between the opinions that step 4 promised.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case being argued about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה and the Shimons argue about whether a מתעסק is liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue about a picker who forgot his intention. Everyone agrees a מתעסק is פטור.

steps.title: They argue only about two categories, but רבי יהודה says they argue about both
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the answer from step 5. According to the Shimons, the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע is only about two categories. רבי יהודה holds that they argue whether it is one category or two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do they argue? About two categories. רבי יהודה holds: it makes no difference whether it is one category or two categories. They argue in both cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes its answer by showing exactly where the Shimons and רבי יהודה disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5 the גמרא said a picker who forgot his plan is חייב according to everyone in the Shimons' view, if it is one category. Now it adds that in the Shimons' view, רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue only when the picker switched to a second category. רבי יהודה says they argue even within one category, so his grapes-and-figs case is not repeating the Shimons after all.
steps.whatToRemember: In the case of a picker who forgot his plan: the Shimons say the argument is only about two categories. רבי יהודה says it is about one category too. Everyone agrees a מתעסק is פטור.

phrases.english: When do they argue? About two categories.
phrases.notes: "They" means רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע, as the Shimons understand them.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds:
It makes no difference whether it is one category
or two categories: they argue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer started in step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case where the opinions differ (the picker who forgot his plan), one category versus two
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה seemed to be saying the same thing as the Shimons, so the difference had to be about a מתעסק
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference is the scope of the argument: two categories only (Shimons) versus both one and two categories (רבי יהודה)

steps.title: רבא: The difference is doing the second act first
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer. The difference between the Shimons and רבי יהודה is a case where the person did his planned acts in the wrong order.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the difference between them is a case of doing something first.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second way to answer רב אושעיא's question. He says the difference between the opinions is about mixing up the order of the acts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's case is someone who planned to pick one fruit first and another second, but picked them in the opposite order. According to the Shimons, רבי יהושע says פטור only if the two fruits are different categories. According to רבי יהודה, רבי יהושע says פטור even if they are the same category.

keyTerms.meaning: To do first, meaning he did the second planned act before the first

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the case of forgetting the plan from step 5. Here he remembers both acts but does them in the wrong order.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The difference between them is doing first.
phrases.notes: He means doing the act he planned to do second before the one he planned to do first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same question, instead of the answer in steps 5-6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different case where the opinions differ: mixing up the order of the acts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference had to be about a מתעסק or about forgetting the plan
steps.terutzMaskana: The opinions differ about someone who did his planned acts in the reverse order

steps.title: A ברייתא about two candles shows that order matters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. If someone meant to put out or light one candle but did it to the other candle, he is פטור. If he meant to light one and put out the other, and did both with one breath, he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: There were two long, lit candles in front of him. He meant to put out this one and put out that one, or meant to light this one and lit that one: he is פטור. If he meant to light and to put out, and he put out and lit with one breath, he is חייב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רבא's idea that the order of the acts makes a difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hitting the wrong candle does not match his plan, so he is פטור. Doing both acts in one breath is חייב, because nothing happened in the wrong order. This hints that if he had really done them in the reverse order, he would be פטור, just as רבא says.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that an act is only counted as a mistaken sin if it matches what the person planned to do, both in what he did and in what order.

phrases.english: And indeed it was taught:
There were two candles in front of him
lit, long ones,
and he meant to put out this one
and he put out that one,

phrases.aramaic: לְהַדְלִיק אֶת זוֹ וְהִדְלִיק אֶת זוֹ – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: or meant to light this one and lit that one: he is exempt.
If he meant to light and to put out,
and he put out and lit with one breath: he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא הָיוּ לְפָנָיו שְׁתֵּי נֵרוֹת דּוֹלְקוֹת אֲרוּכּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רבא's idea that order matters
steps.raayaObject: רבא's idea that doing planned acts in the reverse order counts as not doing what he planned
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: the case of two candles, the wrong candle and the one breath

steps.title: Isn't the one-breath ruling obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the last ruling: he did both things he planned, so of course he is חייב. Why does the ברייתא need to say it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ending of the ברייתא as saying something we already know. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He planned to light and to put out, and he did both. It seems clear that he is חייב, so the ruling looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why say it?

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the need for the last line of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that one breath which puts out and lights makes him חייב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His act matched his plan, so the ruling seems too obvious to need saying

steps.title: It is needed because the order might seem reversed
steps.stepSummary: We might think he is פטור, since he planned to light first but the putting out seems to come first. The ברייתא teaches that since both happened together, nothing came out of order, so he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: his plan was not carried out. He wanted to light first and put out at the end, but when he did the act, he put out first and lit at the end. So I would say he is פטור. The ברייתא teaches us: even though he did not do the lighting first, he also did not do it later.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ruling is needed. Without it, we might think the order was reversed and he is פטור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one breath, the flame is put out on one candle before it lights the other, so it looks like the reverse of his plan. The ברייתא tells us that both happen together, and the lighting was not delayed. Since his plan was not actually reversed, he is חייב. This also supports רבא: a real reversal would make him פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (a mistaken first thought)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, doing planned acts in the reverse order counts as not matching the plan. Doing them at the same time is not a reversal, so he is חייב.

phrases.english: You might have said:
his plan was not carried out,
since he wanted to light first
and to put out at the end,
but when he did the act,
he put out first and lit at the end,
so I would say he is exempt,
it teaches us:
even though he did not do it first,
phrases.notes: "It" is the lighting, which he planned to do first.

phrases.english: he also did not do it later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא question from step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows the mistaken first thought that the ruling comes to reject
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With one breath the putting out comes first, so the order is reversed and he is פטור
steps.terutzMaskana: Both acts happen together, so his plan was not reversed and he is חייב

steps.title: Stoking coals on שבת: one חטאת or two
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: one who stokes coals on שבת brings one חטאת. רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק says two, for putting out the top coals and lighting the bottom ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: One who stirs coals on שבת brings a חטאת. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says in the name of רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק: he brings two, because he puts out the upper coals and lights the lower coals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about stirring coals on שבת. There are two opinions about how many חטאות the person brings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When you stir coals, the top ones get pushed down and go out, and the bottom ones come up and catch fire. The תנא קמא counts this as only one חיוב. רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק counts two separate מלאכות: מכבה (putting out) and מבעיר (lighting).

keyTerms.meaning: sin offering brought for doing a forbidden act by mistake
puts out a fire (a מלאכה of שבת)
lights a fire (a מלאכה of שבת)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who stokes coals on Shabbat
is liable to bring a sin offering.
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Tzadok:
He is liable to bring two,
because he extinguishes the upper ones,
and kindles the lower ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after the discussion of the two candles. The topic is still one action that does two מלאכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: one חטאת for stoking coals. רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק: two חטאות, one for putting out and one for lighting.

steps.title: What case is this? Either way one opinion seems hard
steps.stepSummary: If he meant both to put out and to light, why does the תנא קמא give only one חטאת? If he did not mean to light, why does רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק give two?
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we talking about? If he means to put out and to light, what is the reason of the one who exempts him from the second? But if he does not mean to light, what is the reason of the one who makes him bring two?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to picture the exact case. Each way it pictures it, one of the two opinions is hard to understand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he wanted both results, he did two full מלאכות on purpose, so the תנא קמא should agree to two. If he did not want the lighting, that is a דבר שאינו מתכוין, so רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק should not give two. Neither picture fits both opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: what case are we dealing with?

steps.confusionAlert: The תנא קמא does say he is חייב one חטאת. When the גמרא says 'the one who exempts,' it means he exempts him from the second חטאת.

phrases.english: What are we dealing with?
If he intends to extinguish and to kindle,
what is the reason of the one who exempts?
phrases.notes: He means the תנא קמא, who exempts him from a second חטאת.

phrases.english: Rather, if he does not intend to kindle,
what is the reason of the one who obligates two?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִי דְּקָא מִיכַּוֵּין לְכַבּוֹת וּלְהַבְעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא in step 11 by asking which case could fit both opinions.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case of the ברייתא in step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma. If he intended both acts, the תנא קמא should agree to two. If he did not intend to light, רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק should not require two.

steps.title: The argument is whether damaging kindling is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר and רבי חנינא: he wanted to put out the top coals and lit the bottom ones on purpose as part of the work. The argument is whether מקלקל בהבערה is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר and רבי חנינא both say: The case is where he meant to put out the upper coals in order to light the lower ones. The תנא קמא holds that one who damages through lighting is פטור, and רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק says he is חייב.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question from step 12. They say he does both acts knowingly, but the lighting is a damaging act (מקלקל) for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he knows about both acts, the question 'why two?' goes away. The real argument is about the lighting. The תנא קמא holds that lighting which only damages (מקלקל) is פטור, so he brings only one חטאת. רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק holds that even damaging lighting is חייב, so he brings two.

keyTerms.meaning: one who does a מלאכה in a damaging way, not a building-up way
the first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the question of מקלקל בהבערה, whether damaging lighting is still חייב, can turn one חטאת into two.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַויְיהוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Chanina both say:
For example, where he intended to extinguish the upper ones
in order to kindle the lower ones,
phrases.notes: He lights the bottom coals knowingly, but what he really wants is the top coals put out. That is why the lighting counts as damaging.

phrases.english: for the first Tanna holds:
one who damages through kindling is exempt,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק אָמַר: חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Tzadok says: liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַויְיהוּ: כְּגוֹן שֶׁנִּתְכַּוֵּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma of step 12 by defining a third kind of case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case so that both acts are known, and moves the argument to whether מקלקל בהבערה is חייב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case must be either full intent for both acts or no intent to light, and neither one fits both opinions.
steps.terutzMaskana: He knowingly does both acts, but the lighting is a damaging act. The תנא קמא exempts damaging lighting, and רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק makes him חייב for it.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן agrees: the case is a blacksmith
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן also says the ברייתא is about a נפח (blacksmith). He adds that until this was said, the reason of the law was not understood.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too רבי יוחנן said: they taught this about a blacksmith. רבי יוחנן said: until now, the reason of this law was not revealed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the answer of step 13 with a statement of רבי יוחנן. He says the ברייתא is talking about a blacksmith.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blacksmith wants the coals put out, so for him lighting the bottom coals is a damaging act. That matches the answer of רבי אלעזר and רבי חנינא. רבי יוחנן adds that the ברייתא only makes sense once you know it is about a blacksmith.
steps.whatToRemember: Stoking coals in the ברייתא is about a blacksmith who wants the coals put out. For him the lighting is מקלקל, and that is the whole argument.

phrases.english: And so too said Rabbi Yochanan:
They taught this about a blacksmith.
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Until here, it was not revealed
phrases.notes: He means that before someone said 'it is about a blacksmith,' nobody understood the ברייתא.

phrases.english: the reason of this law.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בְּנַפָּח שָׁנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 13 with רבי יוחנן's agreeing statement.
steps.raayaObject: The answer of רבי אלעזר and רבי חנינא that the case is one where the lighting is a damaging act.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's statement that the ברייתא was taught about a blacksmith.

steps.title: Another pair of אמוראים begins a different explanation
steps.stepSummary: אמי בר אבין and רב חנניא בר אבין are introduced as both saying another explanation. Their words come next.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמי בר אבין and רב חנניא בר אבין both say:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only sets up the next move. Two more אמוראים are about to give another explanation of the ברייתא, and their words come right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we have the 'blacksmith' answer. Now the גמרא opens a second answer to the question of step 12. We will only see what they say in the next part.

phrases.aramaic: אַמֵּי בַּר אָבִין וְרַב חֲנַנְיָא בַּר אָבִין
phrases.english: Ami bar Avin and Rav Chananya bar Avin
both say:

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמֵּי בַּר אָבִין וְרַב חֲנַנְיָא בַּר אָבִין דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַויְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a second answer to the question of step 12, separate from the answer in steps 13 and 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduction to another way of defining the case. The content continues afterward.
